term: causing an event, causing existence, and explaining existence
resolution: The #487 theorem treats Kantian world-relative Causes as a stipulated predecessor relation among individuals present somewhere in one complete possible history. Its root-inclusive rule can be read as existential grounding only under an independently justified interpretation; it is not equivalent to the efficient cause of an event, a temporal beginning, or an explanation token. A beginningless contingent concrete being and an uncaused initial contingent reality are not excluded by weaker event-only or boundary-exception principles. An abstract reason does not meet the typed concrete-predecessor clause. The model supplies literal cross-world identity, not a counterpart policy.
